Dear Margaret,

Thank you for your gift of $15,000 — your first to our newsroom, and one that arrived at a moment when it mattered.

Your support went directly into our county-government desk. Since August, that desk has covered eleven consecutive commission meetings, including the two where the sanitation contract was awarded without public comment. Our reporter was the only journalist in the room for both. The follow-up reporting prompted the commission to reopen the item at its November session.

That is the unglamorous work local accountability depends on, and it is the hardest kind to fund. Meetings do not generate headlines until they do. Donors who fund the seat in the room, rather than the story that comes out of it, are the reason the seat exists.

We were introduced to you through Peter Ashford, and we are glad of it. I would welcome the chance to show you the newsroom this autumn — the team would like to meet the person who backed the beat.

With thanks,

Director of Development

Narrative Report — Civic News Fund
Period: January–December 2026
Grant: $400,000 over two years

Purpose

The grant funds a four-person civic news desk covering municipal government, elections administration, and public spending across the metropolitan region.

What we accomplished

The desk was fully staffed by the end of March, one month behind our projected timeline. Across the year it published 214 pieces, including a nine-part investigation into deferred maintenance in the public housing authority that has since been cited in two city council hearings. Our coverage of the March primary reached an audience of 340,000 unique readers, our highest for any election period.

What did not go to plan

We under-delivered on Spanish-language distribution. The bilingual editor we budgeted for withdrew after accepting another position, and the role sat open for five months. Translated coverage resumed in September at roughly half the volume we projected. We have since restructured the role to report to the managing editor and expect to be at full volume by the second quarter.

The year ahead

The desk enters its second year intact, which in this market is itself an outcome. Our focus is the 2027 municipal election cycle and completing the housing authority series. We will file the January narrative report on schedule.

We are grateful for the Corporation's continued partnership, and for the patience shown during the hiring delay.

Dear Colleague,

Thank you for your continued partnership with our newsroom.

Your support sustains reporting that would not otherwise exist — the municipal meetings covered, the records requested, the follow-up questions asked after everyone else has left the room. Local accountability journalism is expensive, slow, and rarely spectacular, and it survives only where funders are willing to back the work rather than the moment.

This year that support helped us keep reporters on beats through a difficult period for the industry. We published consistently, we held our audience, and we ended the year with the team intact.

We would welcome the chance to talk about what the coming year holds, and where your support can do the most good.

With thanks,

Director of Development
